title: ADC-GS anchor motion Mirror bank
hypothesis: A compact anchor-group × time motion coordinate over shared ADC-GS anchor deformation state can express multiple useful dynamic functions at lower actual serialized bytes than separate motion/deformation state, while retaining quality and rendering throughput.
physical_object: Shared ADC-GS anchor-based Gaussian representation and native hierarchical deformation model
mirror_coordinate: Compact anchor-group × time motion coordinate m
logical_multiplicity: Distinct useful temporal motion trajectories sharing anchor deformation state
controls_required: Shared ADC-GS anchors with ordinary learned motion/time embedding plus deformation decoder
Independent per-motion Gaussian/deformation assets when practical

quality.success_gate: Not frozen; lock thresholds and fresh cells before any evaluation.

blocker: Official ADC-GS setup pins CUDA 11.6-era PyTorch and compiles CUDA Gaussian rasterizer/simple-knn extensions; train/render code calls CUDA directly. Current runtime is CPU-only and no HyperNeRF/N3V scenes or checkpoints are present.
boundaries: Feasibility review only; no model training, rendered quality, payload, or FPS result.
Do not substitute a CPU toy renderer or generic motion field and call MA-897 complete.
